summary: Jackson County, WI lookout first documented by 1932; the current 68-foot tower dates later, its cab was replaced in 2008, and the state network ended in 2015-2016.

facts.design: 68-foot Wisconsin standard model with cage-protected ladder; an earlier 72-foot Baker Improved Strengthened type tower stood by 1932

events.note: Lookout tower in place by 1932 (72-foot Baker Improved Strengthened type tower)
Cab replaced after years of vandalism
Staffed intermittently during spring fire season until 2015 per the register
Statewide network decommissioned; register and WJFW say 2015; Journal Sentinel (Dec. 17, 2015) reported removal from service in 2016

evidence.supports: Lookout towers atop Knapp Mound since at least 1932
evidence.quote: Lookout towers have been atop Knapp Mound dating back to at least 1932.

evidence.supports: Early tower was 72 feet tall, of the Baker Improved Strengthened type

evidence.quote: the tower was in service and staffed intermittently during spring fire season until 2015
until 2015 when Wisconsin decommissioned its lookout network

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and WJFW say the statewide network ended in 2015. The Journal Sentinel reported in December 2015 that the 72 towers would be taken out of service in 2016. The story gives both dates and does not pick one.

notes_for_editor: No source gives the year the current 68-foot tower was built. The La Crosse Tribune Jackson County article (a search hit on local decommissioning) returned HTTP 429 twice and the 2015 Post-Crescent article returned 403, so neither was read. The register's 'Administered by Wisconsin Department of Natural Resources' may be stale given the statewide decommissioning; worth checking who now owns the site. The statewide decisions in the newspaper and WPR pieces are not Knapp-specific, and the story says so. The brief's record for this tower has no errors found.
